column3: “The cry of distress” is rendered “outcry,” and “their countrymen the Jews” as “their Jewish brothers.”
NASB supplies “therefore.” Some read the first clause as “we are mortgaging”; NASB keeps the Hebrew “we … are many.”
“In the famine” is rendered “because of the famine.”
“There is not to the power of our hand” is rendered “we are helpless”; NASB adds “already.”
“It burned to me exceedingly” is rendered “I was very angry.”
“My heart considered with me” is rendered “I consulted with myself,” and “officials” as “rulers.” “Lending usury” is rendered “exacting usury,” and “on them” as “against them.”
“Bought” is rendered “redeemed,” and “according to the sufficiency in us” as “according to our ability.” NASB turns the second clause into a question.
“From the reproach” is rendered “because of the reproach.”
“As this day” is rendered “this very day,” “the hundred” as “the hundredth part,” and “lending” as “exacting.”
“My bosom” is rendered “the front of my garment,” and “carry out” as “fulfill.” “Manner” is rendered “promise.”
“Brothers” is rendered “kinsmen,” and “the food of the governor” as “the governor's food allowance.”
“Made heavy on” is rendered “laid burdens on,” and “after” as “besides.”
“Between ten days in all wine to abundance” is rendered “once in ten days all sorts of wine were furnished in abundance.” “Service” is rendered “servitude.”
